keyframe_review.note: Peloponnese plus central Greece (116 grid cells, 36,133 km2) and, in the Cliopatria shape, seven cells of western Crete. Consistent with the revolt's gains on the page: Phocis revolted 24 March 1821, Livadeia captured 31 March 1821, Tripolitsa seized 23 September 1821, Acrocorinth surrendered 14 January 1822. The page gives no infobox area. Crete: the Egyptian fleet reached Souda Bay on 28 May 1822 and the Cretan revolt failed 'because of Egyptian intervention'; the Cretan cells are kept as unverified.

Central Greece and Crete drop out (49 cells lost, 1 added). The page dates the 1824 destruction of Kasos and Psara but not the Ottoman recapture of central Greece, so the shape stands as Cliopatria's; the ledger records the loss at confidence 1.

minus.text: Missolonghi, whose city fell in 1826; valid from 1826, the shape unchanged for 1825

correction.text: the 1825 shape without Missolonghi from 1826 (Athens also fell in 1827, but the page gives no date)

keyframe_review.note: 1825: Ibrahim lands in February 1825 and 'brought most of the peninsula under Egyptian control by the end of that year'; Cliopatria removes 26 Peloponnese cells in 1825 and regains 18 in Attica-Boeotia-Aetolia. The shape runs to 1827 but Missolonghi fell in 1826 ('the failed naval blockade-breaking in 1826 led to the fall of the city'), so from 1826 the correction removes it.

correction.text: the Peloponnese and central Greece of 1828 without Crete, which the infobox lists as 'ceded to Egypt'

keyframe_review.note: The shape (41,408 km2) regains the Peloponnese and central Greece after 'the Egyptian army withdrew under pressure from a French expeditionary force' in 1828 and the revolutionaries 'retook central Greece'. It also contains 16 cells of Crete, but the page's infobox says 'Crete ceded to Egypt' and that the revolt failed 'because of Egyptian intervention', so Crete is removed.

Independence was recognised on 3 February 1830 (infobox 'Recognition of Independence'; 'London Protocol of February 1830'). The shape is the 1828 land plus a few cells in Euboea and Attica (18 added, 6 lost); Crete again removed (Crete ceded to Egypt, Greek War of Independence infobox). The Arta-Volos extension belongs to 1832 (see next shape).

correction.text: the same shape, valid from 1832: the new kingdom's boundaries 'along the Arta-Volos line'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria begins this shape in 1834, but the Treaty of Constantinople of 21 July 1832 set the kingdom's boundaries 'along the Arta-Volos line' (14 cells added in Aetolia-Acarnania and Phthiotis, Crete's 16 cells removed). The shape should hold from 1832, not 1834; the shape itself is unchanged. 43,999.8 km2; the page gives no area.
No territorial change from 1832 to 1863 on the pages opened (one cell differs from the 1834 shape); the 1862 ousting of King Otto (23 October 1862) is a change of ruler, not of borders.

The shape adds the Ionian Islands (six cells): 'On 21 May 1864 the British departed and the Ionian Islands became three provinces of the Kingdom of Greece' (treaty signed 29 March 1864). Cerigo (Kythira) was also one of the islands.

Same land as 1864 (the 1866 row only drops a stray vertex). Its years should end in 1880: Thessaly and the Arta prefecture were ceded by the Convention of Constantinople of 2 July 1881, which Cliopatria draws from 1885. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1866..1880 from this entry's own 'valid 1866-1880 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the same shape, valid from 1881 (Thessaly apart from Elassona, and the Arta Prefecture)

keyframe_review.note: The shape adds Thessaly and Arta (59 cells, 14,921 km2) but starts in 1885; the page dates the cession to the convention of 2 July 1881 ('Thessaly, apart from Elassona, and a part of southern Epirus (the Arta Prefecture)'). Shape right, years should be 1881-1907. Area 64,329 km2 against the 64,790 km2 the Treaty of Bucharest page gives for Greece before the Balkan Wars (ratio 0.99).

Adds Crete (the Cretan State's 16 cells, 69,828 km2) from 1908, following the Cretan State dossier (union declared unilaterally in October 1908). The Kingdom of Greece page puts the declaration of enosis in the 1908 crisis; the Treaty of Bucharest page says Crete was 'definitively assigned to Greece and taken over on 14 December 1913', so the 1908-1913 Greek control of Crete is a declared union, not an administered one. Area vs the 64,790 km2 infobox figure for pre-1912 Greece: 1.08, plus Crete.

correction.text: the 1912 shape without the Ioannina district and Samos, which fell in March 1913

keyframe_review.note: Balkan War gains in one year (103,441 km2; 110 cells added: Epirus, Macedonia with Thessaloniki, the Aegean islands). Preveza fell 21 October 1912 and Thessaloniki surrendered on 9 November 1912, but 'Ioannina taken on 6 March' and Samos 'securely in Greek hands by 16 March' are 1913, so the 1912 shape without them.

113,618 km2 against the Treaty of Bucharest page's 108,610 km2 for Greece after the war (ratio 1.05). Adds eastern Macedonia (36 cells: 'The Greek-Bulgarian border moved east to beyond Kavala'). Crete was taken over 14 December 1913 and the north-eastern Aegean islands were recognised in February 1914; both are in the shape from 1913.

Unverified: page budget. The shape loses 18 cells in eastern Macedonia (23.35-24.77 E, 41.06-41.49 N) against 1913-1915; no page opened explains it. Recorded as an occupation at confidence 1 in the ledger.

Unverified: page budget. Ten further cells in the northern Aegean (24.62-26.44 E, 38.46-40.64 N) are missing against 1916; no page opened explains it (a gap-filler should open 'National Schism' and 'Macedonian front').
Unverified: page budget. Same land as 1917 (102,576 km2).

Back to the 1913 land plus Western Thrace (51 cells added over 1917-1918): the Treaty of Neuilly (27 November 1919) made Bulgaria 'cede Western Thrace to the Entente', which 'awarded it to Greece at the San Remo conference' (no date on the page), so Greek rule may begin in 1920 rather than 1919.

correction.text: the same shape, with the Anatolian part drawn as occupied land (hatched) and Greece, Western and Eastern Thrace as direct land

keyframe_review.note: 206,605 km2: Greece, Eastern Thrace to the Chatalja lines ('Treaty of Sevres ... ceding Thrace up to the Chatalja lines to Greece', 10 August 1920, never ratified) and the zone in western Anatolia, which was occupied rather than annexed (Smyrna 'under Greek administration, though sovereignty nominally stayed with the Sultan'). The extent is right; the Anatolian part (Smyrna, Manisa, Aydin, Balikesir, Bursa, Usak) should be drawn as occupation, the rest as direct Greek land.

correction.text: the 1922 shape without Eastern Thrace, evacuated under the Armistice of Mudanya (the Lausanne year is not on the pages opened)

keyframe_review.note: 1922-1923 keeps Eastern Thrace (68 cells) although the Armistice of Mudanya (11 October 1922, effective 15 October) required the Greeks 'to evacuate eastern Thrace'; the Anatolian zone is already gone (232 cells lost after the Turkish entry into Smyrna on 9 September 1922). Eastern Thrace is removed.
121,195 km2: Greece within its Neuilly-Lausanne frontier. The republic was proclaimed on 25 March 1924; the page mentions no frontier change in 1924-1940.
Two cells fewer than 1924 (119,501 km2); no frontier change on the page, so the difference is treated as boundary cleanup.
Three cells fewer than 1932 (118,452 km2); no frontier change on the page (Metaxas regime from 4 August 1936).
Same as 1936. 'Italian troops crossed the border on 28 October 1940' (Greco-Italian War). Cliopatria draws nothing for Greece in 1941-1944.

region.text: central administration formed at the First National Assembly of Epidaurus in early 1822: the revolutionary Peloponnese and central Greece

ledger.note: 1822: the Greek revolutionaries proclaim independence ('Proclamation of Independence: 1 January 1822') and form a central administration 'at the First National Assembly of Epidaurus in early 1822'. The page names no frontier; the core is Cliopatria's 1822 shape (Peloponnese, central Greece), which fits the Greek War of Independence page's captures: Livadeia 31 March 1821, Tripolitsa 23 September 1821, Acrocorinth 14 January 1822.

region.text: the land held in 1822 and not in 1824: central Greece north of Attica and western Crete (the shape's own difference)

ledger.note: 1824: central Greece and the Cretan holdings drop out of the Cliopatria shape. Page silent: the Greek War of Independence page dates 'the capture and destruction of Kasos and Psara in 1824' (islands, not in the shape) but not the Ottoman recapture of central Greece.

region.text: most of the peninsula brought under Egyptian control by the end of 1825

ledger.note: February 1825: Ibrahim's Egyptian army lands in the Peloponnese. 'Ibrahim landed in February 1825, and the army brought most of the peninsula under Egyptian control by the end of that year.'

region.text: the Peloponnese cells held in 1824 and not in 1825 (the south-west, 21.4-23.1 E, 36.9-38.1 N)

ledger.note: 1825: the south-west Peloponnese passes to the Egyptian-Ottoman army. 'brought most of the peninsula under Egyptian control by the end of that year'; the Cliopatria shape drops 26 Peloponnese cells in 1825 (the page does not name them).

region.text: the city of Missolonghi

ledger.note: 1826: Missolonghi falls. 'the failed naval blockade-breaking in 1826 led to the fall of the city'; the Cliopatria shape of 1825-1827 still includes it.

1827: the Third National Assembly at Troezen establishes the Hellenic State. 'From 1822 until 1827, it was known as the Provisional Administration of Greece. In 1827, the Third National Assembly at Troezen established the Hellenic State.' Nafplio is the capital 'officially from 1827'.

region.text: the Morea after the Egyptian withdrawal and central Greece retaken

ledger.note: 1828: the Peloponnese and central Greece are retaken. 'In 1828, the Egyptian army withdrew under pressure from a French expeditionary force'; the Ottoman garrisons in the Peloponnese then surrendered and the revolutionaries 'retook central Greece'.

region.text: the Peloponnese and central Greece, fought over since 1825

ledger.note: September 1829: the fighting ends with the Russo-Turkish war. The Porte accepted 'Greek autonomy in the Treaty of Adrianople' (infobox end of the war 12 September 1829; 'Recognition of Autonomy: 22 March 1829' on the First Hellenic Republic page).

3 February 1830: independence recognised. 'Recognition of Independence: 3 February 1830' (First Hellenic Republic page); 'Greece was recognized as an independent state under the London Protocol of February 1830' (Greek War of Independence page). Crete, in the infobox's words, was 'ceded to Egypt'.

1832: Greece becomes a kingdom under the Bavarian prince Otto. The Kingdom of Greece infobox gives 7 May 1832 (the Treaty of London between Bavaria and the protecting Powers); the First Hellenic Republic page gives 'Kingdom established: 30 August 1832' (the date the Powers ratified the Constantinople terms in the London Protocol).

region.text: land inside the Arta-Volos line and outside the 1830 shape

ledger.note: 21 July 1832: the Treaty of Constantinople fixes the northern frontier 'along the Arta-Volos line', the 14 cells Cliopatria adds in Aetolia-Acarnania and Phthiotis (Cliopatria draws them from 1834). The page notes the earlier 'Aspropotamos-Spercheios line' was less favourable; the Ottoman Empire 'was indemnified in the sum of 40,000,000 piastres for the loss of the territory'.
1834: the capital moves from Nafplio to Athens ('Nafplio (1832-1834); Athens (1834-1973)').
23 October 1862: King Otto is ousted; the Danish prince George becomes king in 1863 (infobox 1863-1913). The state and its colour continue.

region.text: the United States of the Ionian Islands (Corfu, Paxos, Santa Maura, Ithaca, Cephalonia, Zante and Cerigo)

ledger.note: 21 May 1864: the Ionian Islands join Greece. The treaty was signed on 29 March 1864 by Charilaos Trikoupis; 'On 21 May 1864 the British departed and the Ionian Islands became three provinces of the Kingdom of Greece.' Counterpart corrected by reviewer eu-18-g: the treaty page names the islands' state as the 'United States of the Ionian Islands', a British protectorate since 1815 (Kingdom of Great Britain ended in 1800); that dossier dissolves into this one in May 1864.

region.text: Thessaly, apart from Elassona, and a part of southern Epirus (the Arta Prefecture)

ledger.note: 2 July 1881: Thessaly and part of Epirus pass to Greece. The Convention of Constantinople was 'signed between the Kingdom of Greece and the Ottoman Empire on 2 July 1881' (new border set by the treaty of 24 May 1881; protocol of the Congress of Berlin, 5 July 1878). Cliopatria draws the land from 1885.

region.text: the island of Crete, the declared union with Greece

ledger.note: October 1908: Crete declares its union with Greece. The Kingdom of Greece page places Venizelos's declaration of enosis in the 1908 crisis; the Cretan State dossier dates the union to October 1908 and Cliopatria draws Crete Greek from 1908. The union was not administered: 'taken over on 14 December 1913' (Treaty of Bucharest page).

region.text: Epirus, Macedonia and the Aegean islands, taken in 1912-1913

ledger.note: October 1912: the First Balkan War opens the Greek front in Epirus and Macedonia. 'Preveza: taken 21 October 1912' (Kingdom of Greece page); the page gives no war-declaration date.

region.text: Preveza

ledger.note: 21 October 1912: Preveza is taken. 'Preveza: taken 21 October 1912.'

region.text: Thessaloniki and its garrison, surrendered 9 November 1912

ledger.note: 9 November 1912: Thessaloniki surrenders. The Ottoman commander 'surrendered Thessaloniki and its garrison of 26,000 men to the Greeks on 9 November'.

region.text: Ioannina and Epirus

ledger.note: 6 March 1913: Ioannina falls. 'Ioannina taken on 6 March' (the Cliopatria 1912 shape already includes the district).

region.text: Samos

ledger.note: 16 March 1913: Samos is Greek. 'Samos securely in Greek hands by 16 March.'

region.text: Epirus, Macedonia and the Aegean islands

ledger.note: March 1913: the fighting on the Greek-Ottoman front ends with Ioannina (6 March) and Samos (16 March); the Treaty of London that ended the war is not dated on the pages opened for Greece.

region.text: eastern Macedonia east of the 1912 line, to beyond Kavala

ledger.note: June 1913: the Second Balkan War. Bulgaria 'attacked its former allies in June 1913'; the front in eastern Macedonia is the land the Greek-Bulgarian border later moved across.

region.text: eastern Macedonia east of the 1912 line, to beyond Kavala

ledger.note: 10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the Second Balkan War ('concluded on 10 August 1913').

region.text: the Greek-Bulgarian border moved east to beyond Kavala

ledger.note: 10 August 1913: Greece gets eastern Macedonia. 'The Greek-Bulgarian border moved east to beyond Kavala'; Greece's area 'rose from 64,790 to 108,610 km2'.

region.text: Crete, definitively assigned to Greece

ledger.note: 14 December 1913: Crete is taken over. 'Crete was definitively assigned to Greece and taken over on 14 December 1913.'

region.text: the north-eastern Aegean islands

ledger.note: February 1914: the Great Powers recognise Greek sovereignty over the north-eastern Aegean islands, 'undetermined until the Great Powers recognized it in February 1914'.

region.text: the cells of eastern Macedonia present in 1913-1915 and absent in 1916

ledger.note: 1916: eastern Macedonia leaves the Greek shape. Page silent: the Cliopatria shape loses 18 cells there (23.35-24.77 E, 41.06-41.49 N); no page opened explains it. The researcher reads it as an occupation by Bulgaria, which a gap-filler should confirm ('Macedonian front', 'National Schism'). Reviewer eu-18-g, Macedonian front page: 'The unopposed Bulgarian advance into Greek-held eastern Macedonia precipitated a crisis in Greece' (offensive launched 17 August 1916); in the east the Bulgarians 'easily conquered all Greek territory east of the river Struma'. Month and source added, confidence raised to 2.

region.text: the same cells, back in the shape

ledger.note: 1919: the eastern Macedonian cells return to the Cliopatria shape. Page silent on the date of the end of the occupation. Reviewer eu-18-g, Macedonian front page: the Bulgarians were 'granted the Armistice of Salonica' on 29 September 1918 and 'The Macedonian front ended at noon on 30 September 1918 when the ceasefire came into effect'; the evacuation date is not on the page, so the end is dated to the armistice (as in the principality-of-bulgaria dossier). Moved from 1919.

region.text: Smyrna and its surroundings

ledger.note: 15 May 1919: Greece lands at Smyrna. 'twenty thousand Greek soldiers landed in Smyrna and took control of the city and its surroundings.'

region.text: Western Thrace (and the eastern Macedonian cells), cut off Bulgaria's Aegean outlet

ledger.note: 27 November 1919: the Treaty of Neuilly takes Western Thrace from Bulgaria. 'The treaty was signed on 27 November 1919'; Bulgaria had 'to cede Western Thrace to the Entente', which 'awarded it to Greece at the San Remo conference' (no date on the page).

region.text: western and northwestern Anatolia: Manisa, Balikesir, Aydin, Bursa, Usak

ledger.note: Summer 1920: Greek offensives extend the zone to Bursa and Usak. 'Greek offensives reached the Buyuk Menderes valley, Bursa, and Alasehir, extending Greek control over most of western and northwestern Anatolia, including Manisa, Balikesir, Aydin, Bursa, and Usak.'

region.text: Thrace up to the Chatalja lines

ledger.note: 10 August 1920: the Treaty of Sevres gives Greece Eastern Thrace. It signed away 'Thrace up to the Chatalja lines to Greece' and put Smyrna 'under Greek administration, though sovereignty nominally stayed with the Sultan'; 'The treaty was never ratified.'

region.text: Smyrna and its surroundings

ledger.note: 9 September 1922: Turkish forces enter Smyrna. The Great Offensive began 26 August 1922; 'The Greek army was defeated at Dumlupinar on 30 August'; 'Turkish forces entered Smyrna' on 9 September after the Greek authorities had left two days earlier.

region.text: western and northwestern Anatolia

ledger.note: September 1922: the whole Anatolian zone is lost (232 Cliopatria cells). The furthest Greek advance had been the Sakarya (23 August-13 September 1921), under 100 km west of Ankara.

region.text: Eastern Thrace, evacuated under the Armistice of Mudanya

ledger.note: 15 October 1922: Eastern Thrace is evacuated. The Armistice of Mudanya was concluded on 11 October 1922 and 'took effect on 15 October'; the Greeks were 'to evacuate eastern Thrace and the Bosporus zones'. Cliopatria keeps the land to 1923; the Lausanne year is not on the pages opened.
25 March 1924: the Second Hellenic Republic is proclaimed. 'Republic proclaimed: 25 March 1924, by Alexandros Papanastasiou.'
10 October 1935: the monarchy is restored. Kondylis 'abolished the Republic in another coup and declared the monarchy restored'; a plebiscite in November 1935 confirmed it.

region.text: the Greek state at the Italian invasion

ledger.note: 1940: Cliopatria's row ends here, not the Greek state. 'Italian troops crossed the border on 28 October 1940.' The Axis occupation of 1941-1944 has no Cliopatria shape for Greece; the state reappears as the Kingdom of Greece row of 1945-1966 (slug kingdom-of-greece, another group). The page opened is silent on 1941.

wars.name: Greek War of Independence

zones.text: the Morea, lost to Ibrahim in 1825 and regained in 1828

wars.outcome: Greek autonomy accepted at Adrianople (September 1829), independence recognised in the London Protocol of February 1830; the Arta-Volos frontier fixed by the Treaty of Constantinople on 21 July 1832.
wars.note: The page gives the French Morea expedition and the Egyptian withdrawal as 1828 without a month and dates Navarino to 1827 without a day. The Egyptian army of Ibrahim belongs to the Muhammad Ali dynasty row (slug muhammad-ali-dynasty, another group); the ledger names the Ottoman Empire as the counterpart because the page speaks of Ottoman garrisons and an Egyptian army together.

wars.name: First Balkan War
wars.outcome: Greece takes Epirus south of the future Albanian frontier, southern Macedonia with Thessaloniki, Crete and the Aegean islands; confirmed by the Treaty of Bucharest of 10 August 1913.
wars.note: Dates are from the Kingdom of Greece page; it does not date the war's start or the Treaty of London.

wars.name: Second Balkan War
wars.outcome: Bulgaria loses; the Greek-Bulgarian border moves east to beyond Kavala; Treaty of Bucharest, 10 August 1913.

wars.name: Greco-Turkish War (1919-1922)
wars.outcome: Greek defeat at Sakarya (1921) and Dumlupinar (30 August 1922); Smyrna lost 9 September 1922; Eastern Thrace evacuated after the Armistice of Mudanya (11 October 1922).
wars.note: The Treaty of Lausanne and the population exchange are mentioned on the page without dates. The Turkish National Movement has no dossier in this batch (counterparts_needing_dossiers).

wars.name: Greco-Italian War
wars.outcome: 'Italian troops crossed the border on 28 October 1940'; the page opened gives no territorial result.
wars.note: Listed so that it is seen to have been considered; no border change is recorded.

certainty.note: A revolutionary front that moved with every campaign; no treaty line until the London Protocol of February 1830, and the Arta-Volos line only in 1832.

The Arta-Volos line of the Treaty of Constantinople (1832) and the border treaty of 24 May 1881 with the convention of 2 July 1881; the Ionian Islands transfer of 1864 is a treaty. Crete 1908-1911 is a declared union, soft.
The Balkan War fronts move monthly; Epirus, Macedonia and the islands harden with the Treaty of Bucharest (10 August 1913).
The Bucharest frontiers; the north-eastern Aegean islands were recognised in February 1914. The Epirus frontier with Albania is not on any page opened.
Occupation and war: eastern Macedonia 1916-1918, the Smyrna zone and Anatolian advance 1919-1922, Eastern Thrace 1920-1922.
The Neuilly and Lausanne frontiers; the Lausanne date is not on the pages opened.

notes:
Budget: nine pages for 23 shapes (the maximum for 12-30 shapes), so the Macedonian front of 1916-1918, the 1897 war, the National Schism, Lausanne and the Cretan State were not opened.

Cliopatria's 'First Hellenic Republic' row is the Greek state for 1822-1940 (First Hellenic Republic to 1832, Kingdom of Greece 1832-1924, Second Hellenic Republic 1924-1935, Kingdom again 1935-). The Wikipedia article of that title covers 1822-1832 only; renames carry the later names. The row resumes as 'Kingdom of Greece' in 1945 (slug kingdom-of-greece): same state, with the 1941-1944 occupation absent from Cliopatria. The dissolve event of 1940 is a technical close of this row (confidence 1), not a dissolution.

Cliopatria errors proposed: (1) Crete in the 1828 and 1830 shapes (16 cells) was held by Egypt, not Greece ('Crete ceded to Egypt'); (2) the Arta-Volos extension belongs to 1832, not 1834; (3) Thessaly and Arta were ceded in 1881, drawn from 1885; (4) the 1922-1923 shape keeps Eastern Thrace after the Mudanya evacuation; (5) the Anatolian zone of 1919-1922 should be hatched occupation, not Greek land; (6) Crete 1908-1913 is a declared union, taken over 14 December 1913 (the Cretan State dossier ends in October 1908, so Crete's status 1908-1913 is for the gap-filler to settle); (7) the 1912 shape includes Ioannina and Samos, which fell in March 1913.

Unexplained: the 1916 loss of eastern Macedonia (recorded as a confidence-1 occupation by Bulgaria, from the researcher's reading, no page opened), the 1917 loss of ten Aegean cells, and the return of both by 1919. The Provisional Government of National Defence (Thessaloniki, 1916-1917) is not opened and has no dossier. The 1920 Anatolian zone also includes cells (Bursa, Usak) beyond the Smyrna zone proper. Counterparts: the Turkish National Movement has no dossier in this batch; the Egyptian army is the Muhammad Ali dynasty row. The Ottoman dossier dates the Greek gain of the Peloponnese and central Greece to 1829 and the contest end to 1830; this dossier follows the 1828 and September 1829 dates of the Greek War of Independence page.

Gazetteer names used that may not resolve: the Preveza, Samos and Missolonghi radii are given by coordinates; 'Western Thrace' and Elassona are not names in the gazetteer (Western Thrace is taken as a Cliopatria difference).

Infobox areas compared (Treaty of Bucharest page): Greece before the Balkan Wars 64,790 km2 against Cliopatria 1885-1907 64,329 km2 (0.99) and 1908-1911 69,828 km2 (1.08, with Crete); after the wars 108,610 km2 against 113,618 km2 (1.05). The Kingdom of Greece infobox gives no area.
